course.title: FatTail Labs: The Operating System
course.subtitle: How the Lab builds habits that stick — Journey, Practice, Wiki, Strategy Lab, and Toughness
course.description_md:
FatTail Labs is not a content dump. It is an **operating system for trader development** — tools and programs that turn daily work into durable habits and skills.

This course is the map. Every lesson starts with a short **intro video**, then **written directions** for the surface you just saw. Watch, then do.

### Two through-lines

**1. Process Flow.** Everything you use in Labs shapes **Process Flow** — the flow state of your trading process. It is a **state of being**, not a test score. Recent behavior matters more than old history. Journey is where that state stays honest and current.

**2. One life.** Trading routines are not a separate identity from the rest of your life. **Toughness** is the life-routines system that makes durable success possible. Hard 20 / 40 / 75 sprints are **training exercises** for mental toughness (associated with the anterior mid-cingulate cortex, aMCC). The routines you build around those exercises become natural as that capacity develops — and your trading loop (log, journal, retrospective) is part of the same life.

**Continuous journaling.** The Journal is not an end-of-day chore. You write with every experience — pre-market analysis, mid-session decisions, trade moments, and post-market exhale. Trade Log holds structure as it happens; Journal holds mind. A day-start routine invites that habit when the trading day begins.

### What you will walk away with

- A clear purpose for FatTail Labs: habits and skills that lead to durable success
- Fluency in Journey and **Process Flow**
- The Practice loop: Trade Log → Journal → Retrospective → Reports
- How Wiki, Strategy Lab, and Toughness fit without drowning you
- Process outcomes only — never profit theater

modules.title: Overview: Why FatTail Labs Exists
modules.description_md: One lesson. The thesis of the Lab before you touch any app.

content_blocks.script_md: Labs purpose: trader development OS; stop the bleeding; capacity over dependency; process outcomes never profit claims; map of Journey / Process Flow / Practice / Wiki / Strategy Lab / Toughness; one life — trading routines are life routines.

content_blocks.body_md:
## What this course is for

FatTail Labs exists to help traders develop **solid habits and skills** that lead to durable success — not to hand you signals or a P&L scoreboard.

### The thesis

- **Stop the bleeding** — capital preservation is the first step for many, and for some the only step they need
- Sell the dream, **sequence the discipline** — pathway routes through process first
- **Capacity over dependency** — tools build *your* judgment
- Speak in **process outcomes** (adherence, drawdown stopped, review cadence) — never profit claims
- **One life** — trading routines are routines you enable in your life, not a costume you wear only during market hours

### The map you will learn

| Surface | Job |
|---------|-----|
| **Journey** | Path + **Process Flow** across everything you use |
| **Practice** | Day-to-day loop: Trade Log → Journal → Retrospective → Reports |
| **Wiki** | Growing map of what we teach |
| **Strategy Lab** | Build / Test / Run with process gates |
| **Toughness** | Life routines and mental toughness; Hard sprints as brain training |

### How each lesson works

1. Short intro video
2. Written directions
3. Do the thing in the app — do not only watch

### Do this now

- [ ] Open **Apps** from the main nav
- [ ] Skim Journey, Practice, and Toughness without changing data yet
- [ ] Write one life habit and one trading habit you want non-negotiable this month

### Not this course

Strategy mechanics live in other courses (0DTE Foundations, Pure Options, Campaigns, …). This course is the **operating system**, not the playbook for a specific structure.

lessons.title: Process Flow — The Flow State of Your Trading

content_blocks.script_md: Process Flow = state of being, not a test score; pillars; key parts weighted; recent data weighted more (exponential average); Establishing for new members; never P&L. UI may still say Process Integrity until rename ships.

content_blocks.body_md:
## What Process Flow is

**Process Flow** is a **state of being** — the **flow state of your trading process**.

It is **not** “the score you got after a test.” It is whether your process is coherent, honest, and **current**.

- **High flow** — habits holding under load; process is present
- **Drifting flow** — process is fragmented or stale; reinstall the routine (no identity attack)
- **Establishing** — new members are not labeled “Poor” for starting; empty ≠ failure

### Why this framing matters

A “score” invites gaming and shame. **Flow** asks: am I in process right now, and is recent life holding the stack?

### How it is measured (member-safe)

1. **Pillars** — parts of process life:
   - Learning rhythm
   - Live presence
   - Practice persistence
   - Daily routine
   - Process adherence (plan-following on tagged trades)
   - Retrospective cadence
   - Mental toughness when you engage Toughness / Hard
2. **Weights** — key quality pillars count for more than pure show-up
3. **Recent emphasis** — exponential average so **more recent weeks weigh more** than old history; drift surfaces; ancient good weeks do not forever prop a broken present
4. **Labels** describe the **state of flow**, not your worth as a person

### What never moves Process Flow

P&L, win rate, profit claims, peer profit rank.

### Do this now

- [ ] Open Journey → Process Flow (or Process Integrity if the UI has not renamed yet)
- [ ] Name your weakest pillar this week
- [ ] One process action (not bigger trade size)

## What to do here

This is a **knowledge check** for Module 2 (The Journey) — not an empty page and not a second course catalog.

1. Read the short recap below (optional if you just finished the prior lessons).
2. **Answer every question** in the quiz on this page.
3. Submit — you get **immediate scoring** and explanations.
4. Results feed your **Journey** learning activity (understanding check, not P&L).

### Recap (what you should already know)

| Idea | Takeaway |
|------|----------|
| **Journey** | Cross-Lab path + Process Flow — not a second product, not a profit leaderboard |
| **Process Flow** | State of being / practice compass (radar) — **not** a test scorecard |
| **Active span** | Calendar silence outside engagement is not failure; process quality **while engaged** matters |
| **Learning path** | Enrollments, resume next lesson, quiz results live on Journey |
| **What never counts** | P&L, win rate, peer profit rank |

When you are ready, scroll to the quiz and begin.

lessons.title: Trade Log — Capture the Experience When It Happens

content_blocks.script_md: Trade Log is a living book of record — log structure as experiences happen, not only tonight's bookkeeping; process framing; bridge to Journal same day.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Open Trade Log

- **Practice → Trade Log** — `/app/trade-log`

### What it is

Options-first blotter: multi-leg fills and structure as **process evidence**. Table-first; open a row in the right-hand sheet to create, edit, or review.

### Continuous practice — not end-of-day only

Log the experience **when it happens** (or as soon as fills land):

1. Confirm **Account** and **Date** in Practice Context
2. Create or import the trade
3. Capture structure, legs, and short process notes on the sheet
4. Open **Journal for the same date** for the thinking (plan, hesitation, rule follow/break) — Trade Log holds structure; Journal holds mind
5. Close positions when done so Reports stay honest

### Import

Imports may arrive after the fact. Still add a **same-day Journal turn** when you review imported fills so the day conversation stays complete.

### Framing

Process and structure first — not a theater of profits.

### Do this now

- [ ] Add one real or practice trade under the correct account
- [ ] Open Journal for that same date and write one line about *why* the trade existed

lessons.title: Journaling Is Continuous — Not End of Day

content_blocks.script_md: Core thesis: journal with every experience through the day; one conversation per date; timestamps; week bands prove when you wrote; never EOD-only habit.

content_blocks.body_md:
## The rule

**Journaling is not something you do at the end of the day.**

Journaling is something you do **with every experience you have throughout the day** — pre-market analysis, decisions mid-session, trade moments, and post-market exhale.

### Open Journal

- **Practice → Journal** — `/app/journal`
- One **conversation per date** — the whole day is one thread
- Every message is **timestamped** — the record shows *when* you wrote
- Composer is always ready — no “start journaling” ceremony

### Why continuous beats EOD-only

| EOD-only | Continuous |
|----------|------------|
| Memory rewrites the day | Intent and emotion stay closer to truth |
| Pre-market plan is lost | Pre-market is still in the thread for Retrospective |
| Process Flow looks sparse | Multiple touches keep process **current** |

### Week view (activity map)

Week view shows **when** you wrote across the day (before the open, morning, afternoon, after the close). Dots mean *you* wrote in that part of the day — not that the agent chatted. Use it to see whether you only dump at night.

### What never belongs in the habit

- Waiting for a perfect essay after the close
- P&L theater as the body of the journal
- Shame for a thin day — sparse is information; rebuild tomorrow

### Do this now

- [ ] Open **today’s** Journal
- [ ] Write one short turn about something that already happened (or is about to — pre-market)
- [ ] Glance at Week view if available — notice which bands have dots

content_blocks.script_md: Pre-market is journal not a separate notebook; capture plan/regime/bias/invalidation before open; post-market is exhale not scorecard; expected vs actual in retro uses pre-open intent.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Pre-market analysis — in the Journal

Before the open, open **today’s** Journal and capture process intent. This is not a second notebook. It is the same conversation.

Suggested beats (plain language — not a form you must complete):

- Regime / volatility read
- Directional bias (if any)
- Levels or invalidation you care about
- What you will **not** do today
- How you will size / risk under the plan

**Why it matters later:** Retrospective can compare **what you intended before the open** with what you actually did. That comparison dies if pre-market only lived in your head.

### During the day

Add short turns when something changes: plan break, hesitation, good follow-through, boredom, revenge urge. Link the Trade Log for structure; put the *why* here.

### Post-market exhale

After the close (or when you stop for the day), one honest turn:

- What held
- What broke
- What you release (no revenge narrative)
- One small commitment for tomorrow

This is an **exhale**, not a trophy room and not a self-attack.

### Do this now

- [ ] If before the open: write today’s pre-market turn now
- [ ] If after the close: write a post-market exhale for the last session you traded or observed
- [ ] If mid-day: write what just shifted in the plan

content_blocks.script_md: Day-start notification invites pre-market Journal; not shame; process only; until product ships use calendar/alarm; deep link Journal today.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Why a trigger

Continuous journaling fails when the day starts in the broker and the Journal never opens. A **day-start routine** invites process first.

### What Labs will do (product direction)

When you start your day, Labs can:

1. Notify you (in-app first; browser later if you allow it)
2. Open **Journal for today** with Practice Context already on today
3. Soft-prompt pre-market (“what’s the plan?”) — never block, never shame
4. Stay quiet if you already wrote before the open

Rules that will not change:

- Process language only — no P&L, no “your score dropped”
- At most one day-start nudge per day
- You can turn it off
- Empty days are not moral failure

### Until notifications ship — build the habit yourself

- [ ] Set a phone/calendar alarm for **prep time** (e.g. 45 minutes before the open)
- [ ] Alarm action: open Labs → Journal → write pre-market
- [ ] Optional second chime after the close for the exhale only

### Do this now

- [ ] Choose your prep time for the next trading day
- [ ] Put it on the calendar with the link or path: Journal / today
- [ ] Write one line: “When the day starts, I open ____ first.”

content_blocks.script_md: Retro uses continuous journal + trades; expected vs actual needs pre-market; process first.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Open Retrospective

- **Practice → Retrospective** — `/app/retrospective`

### What it is

Structured review: what held, what broke, what you commit next. Process first; results secondary — never the headline as a brag.

### Why continuous journaling feeds retro

- Pre-market turns give **expected vs actual** something real to compare
- Mid-day turns explain discretionary choices without hindsight fiction
- Trade Log supplies structure; Journal supplies mind
- Post-market exhale seeds the next week’s commitments

### Surfaces

- **Library** of past retrospectives
- **Scope** — from last review (or maiden journey)
- **Ceremony** — cause, what worked, next commitments
- **Cadence** — gentle nudges when a review is due

### Do this now

- [ ] If you have about a week of continuous notes: start a Retrospective
- [ ] If not: keep the day-thread habit until the first retro date

## Open Reports

### What it is

How the selected account’s path evolved. Drawdown as **capital path risk**, not a trophy. Tables from Trade Log.

### How to use it

1. Match **Account** to the book you care about
2. Read path and drawdown before strategy tables
3. Drill into fills when a number needs the blotter
4. Take one fact into Journal or the next Retrospective — numbers serve process, they do not replace it

### Do this now

- [ ] Open Reports for your primary practice account
- [ ] Note one path or drawdown fact for Journal or the next retro

content_blocks.script_md: Full loop continuous journal + trade log → retro → reports → Process Flow; Playbook coming.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Playbook (when it ships)

Personal defined-risk setups and rules. Until then: rules in **Journal**, structures in **Trade Log**.

### Close the loop

```
Day-start → Journal (pre-market)
    → Trade Log + Journal turns through the session
        → Journal (post-market exhale)
            → Retrospective (weekly judgment)
                → Reports (path honesty)
                    → Process Flow on Journey (state of being)
```

### Do this now

- [ ] Name the continuous loop out loud without looking at this page
- [ ] Schedule tomorrow’s prep time

content_blocks.body_md:
## Open Strategy Lab

- **Apps → Strategy Lab**

### What it is

The place to **build**, **test**, and **run** strategies with **process gates**. It extends practice — it does not replace Trade Log honesty or Process Flow.

### Three modes

| Mode | Job |
|------|-----|
| **Build** | Define structure, rules, and constraints |
| **Test** | Historical / simulated evaluation before you trust it |
| **Run** | Live or paper execution under gates you accept |

### Honest boundaries

- Not “someone else’s picks”
- Capacity stays with you: you own the rules and the review
- What is live vs coming depends on your environment — do not invent features

### Do this now

- [ ] Open Strategy Lab and identify Build / Test / Run entry points
- [ ] Note what is live vs coming where you are

content_blocks.script_md: Lab fills → Trade Log; Journal promotion Test→Run; retro includes discretion; Process Flow; gate yourself.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Closing the loop

- Tests and runs should still produce **Trade Log** evidence when they fill
- Journal the decision to promote a strategy from Test → Run
- Retrospective includes bot and manual discretion the same way: process first

### Process Flow

Meaningful Lab use shapes overall standing. Skipping Practice while “only running bots” is still process drift.

### Gate yourself

- [ ] Written rules before Run
- [ ] Test evidence before size
- [ ] Retro after a defined sample — not after a lucky day

### Do this now

- [ ] Write one promotion criterion you refuse to skip (for example: N test days)

modules.title: The Toughness Program
modules.description_md: Toughness is the life-routines system for durable success. Hard 20/40/75 are training exercises for mental toughness (aMCC). Trading process is one family of life routines — not a separate life.

lessons.title: Toughness Is Life Routines — Not Just Sprints

content_blocks.script_md: Toughness = overall life routines and habits for ultimate success; sprints are one tool; mental toughness lexicon; not a profit program; not medical advice.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Open Toughness

- **Apps → Toughness**

### The real program

Toughness is the **overall life routines and habits** you construct so follow-through becomes who you are — sleep, training, food, recovery, review, community, and the trading process you keep when nobody is watching.

That architecture supports durable success. The calendar sprints are **not** the destination.

### What the sprints are (preview)

- **Hard 20 / 40 / 75** = deliberate **training exercises**
- They train **mental toughness** under voluntary difficulty
- They sit *inside* the life-routine system; they do not replace it

### What Toughness is not

- Not “I finished 75 so I’m done”
- Not a profit program or signal service
- Not a substitute for medical care, therapy, or rest when those are what you need
- Not a shame machine for missing a day

### Product lexicon

Member UI: **mental toughness** / **Hard** — not “tenacity” branding.

### Do this now

- [ ] Open the Toughness hub and skim the whole surface, not only enroll buttons
- [ ] List 3–5 **life** routines you already depend on (or need)
- [ ] Mark which are solid vs aspirational — before you touch a sprint

lessons.title: Training the Brain — aMCC and Mental Toughness

content_blocks.script_md: aMCC / willpower framing (paraphrase + cite Touroutoglou et al. 2020 Cortex); mental toughness = persisting when effort is costly; Hard = repeated voluntary challenge; no guaranteed aMCC growth.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Why the sprints exist

Hard and related deliberate-challenge protocols train **persistence and willpower** — **mental toughness** — by repeating voluntary difficulty.

Literature associates that capacity with the **anterior mid-cingulate cortex (aMCC)** (sometimes popularized as a “willpower muscle”). Product maps the paper’s “tenacity” language to **mental toughness** in member UI.

### What we tell you (honest shape)

1. **What** is trained: mental toughness — persisting when effort is costly
2. **Where** literature situates it: **aMCC**
3. **How** Labs applies it: repeated voluntary challenge (Hard ladder)
4. **What is not claimed:** we do **not** guarantee your aMCC will grow, thicken, or “level up”
5. Attribute, paraphrase — e.g. Touroutoglou et al., 2020, *Cortex*; do not invent papers

### Honest science posture

- Education, not diagnosis
- 75 Hard / selection culture = practice analogues, not peer-reviewed proof that Labs rewired anyone’s cortex

### The developmental claim that *is* on-thesis

As you train under load, the **routines you build around the sprints** become more **natural**. That is the point: capacity in life, not a badge.

### Do this now

- [ ] Read the hub’s physiology / how-it-works cite block once, slowly
- [ ] Complete: “I am training mental toughness so that ____ becomes easier without willpower theater.”

lessons.title: Routines Around the Sprints Become Who You Are

content_blocks.script_md: Sprint is stimulus; surrounding stack is the real win; naturalization as capacity develops; design your day before you enroll.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Stimulus vs system

| Piece | Role |
|-------|------|
| **Sprint days** | Training load — deliberate difficulty |
| **Routines around the sprint** | Sleep window, movement, meals, shutdown, review, who you tell |
| **What sticks** | The stack becomes default as capacity grows — not the selfie of day 75 |

### Design the stack first

Before enrolling, answer:

1. When do I sleep and wake on a hard day?
2. What movement / challenge rules am I actually running?
3. When do I review (Journal / retro) relative to market hours?
4. What happens when life hits (travel, illness, family)?

### Naturalization

- Early days: high friction, high intention
- Later: the same actions cost less internal argument — that is the training working in life
- If the stack is fantasy, the sprint only produces burnout

### Do this now

- [ ] Write a one-page **life stack** for a Hard day (morning → market → evening)
- [ ] Circle the item most likely to break; redesign it before you enroll

content_blocks.script_md: No split life: log, journal, retro = same kind of routine as training/sleep; Practice apps are how trading routines live in software; Toughness trains capacity that keeps those routines when markets are boring or painful.

content_blocks.body_md:
## One life, one capacity

Trading routines are **not separate from your life**. They are routines you **enable** the same way you enable training days, sleep, and recovery.

| Life routine | Trading twin in Labs |
|--------------|----------------------|
| Show up when it’s hard | Log the trade you don’t want to look at |
| Honest review | Journal + Retrospective |
| Track the path | Reports + Process Flow on Journey |
| Protect body and mind | Position size, stop the bleeding, no revenge spiral |

### What this ends

- “I’m disciplined at the gym but chaotic in the book” as two identities
- Treating Practice apps as homework for a persona that only exists 9:30–4:00

### What this starts

- Same mental toughness for boring process as for hard workouts
- Journey as a read on **whole-life process**, not trader cosplay

### Do this now

- [ ] Name one non-trading routine that already works for you
- [ ] Attach one trading twin (same time block or same non-negotiable rule)
- [ ] Put the pair in Journal for this week

content_blocks.script_md: How-it-works; ladder 20/40/75 as progressive training load; miss → day one; life still happens; start lower than ego; sprints serve the life stack.

content_blocks.body_md:
## Placement

Enroll only after you understand Toughness as life routines + aMCC-framed training. Sprints are the **gym set**, not the life.

### The ladder (training load)

| Program | Shape | Training intent |
|---------|--------|-----------------|
| **Hard 20** | Entry load | Prove you can start and finish a short block |
| **Hard 40** | Stretch load | Consistency under more days |
| **Hard 75** | Peak optional | Only after lower rungs hold in *life*, not just on a calendar |

True 75 Hard (Andy Frisella’s program) may also appear on the hub as-is with optional tracking — separate from FatTail Hard lengths.

### How it works

1. Watch how-it-works on the hub
2. Confirm your **life stack** is realistic
3. Choose the lowest rung that still challenges you
4. Track daily honestly (Today’s log)
5. **Miss or fail a required task → day one** (product rule — explain without shame theater)
6. Life still happens; know the rules before you enroll

### Ladder psychology

Completing 20 with a real stack beats failing 75 for applause. The win is **capacity and natural routines**, not the number on a badge.

### Do this now

- [ ] If not ready: stay in life-stack design + Practice loop — no forced enroll
- [ ] If ready: enroll in the lowest honest rung; put the first week’s stack on the calendar

- Life stack first, badge second

6. **Toughness** — life routines + aMCC training; trading routines as life routines

**Next action:** one honest life or trading rep today — then check Journey tomorrow.
